title: Lean Marketing | What Is a Joint Venture?

facts.fact: The article 'What Is a Joint Venture?' was published on January 15, 2025, by Allan Dib.
The page lists an estimated reading time of 7 minutes for the article.
The page defines a joint venture as a arrangement in which two parties combine resources with a complementary, non-competitive business to achieve a particular goal.
facts.quote: A joint venture is created when two parties combine resources with a complimentary, non-competitive business to achieve a particular goal.

facts.fact: According to the page, a joint venture lets both companies keep their separate business structure and legal status while building a jointly-owned entity.
facts.quote: This alliance allows both companies to maintain their separate business structure and legal status while building a jointly-owned entity.

facts.fact: The page states that four key factors differentiate a partnership from a joint venture.
facts.quote: Four key factors differentiate a partnership from a joint venture.

facts.fact: The page says a partnership is legally bound and requires an agreement setting out its terms, whereas a joint venture does not require a written agreement.
facts.quote: A partnership is legally bound. This requires an agreement that explains the terms and conditions of the partnership. On the other hand, having an agreement on paper is not a requirement for a joint venture.

facts.fact: The page states that a joint venture typically has a shorter duration than a partnership because it aims at a particular goal.
facts.quote: a joint venture typically has a shorter duration since it only aims at a particular goal.

facts.fact: The page states that in a joint venture, partners share campaign expenses, which puts less financial burden on each party.
facts.quote: In a joint venture, you'll share expenses with your partner on a project or campaign, putting less of a financial burden on you.
